Hi Anika / Tom,

Thanks again for carving out time today — great discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the technical constraints you shared, and proposed next steps from Redwood to validate fit. Goal is to lock the deployment topology and SLO targets so Marcus & Neha can scope a draft architecture + pricing.

1) Key pain points you reiterated
- Unpredictable inference latency spikes during EMR-parsing bursts (affects provider workflows).
- Unit cost and token spend growth during batch analysis windows.
- Need for private network options (PHI guards) and auditability for compliance.

2) Goals / success criteria (as we captured)
- p95 response <= 350 ms for 512-token prompts (clinical summarization path).
- p99 <= 750 ms for the same path during steady-state; graceful degradation on burst.
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,200 requests/hour for the summarization route (~average 450 tokens per request).
- Audit logs retained for 180 days, with KMS-integrated key management.

3) Model requirements you called out
- Prefer open-weight model (no vendor lock) with 16-bit and quantized 8-bit options — target initial evaluation with a 13B-class model, then 70B for higher-fidelity triage.
- KV cache reuse across sessions is useful for identical patient note prefixes.
- Deterministic output for certain templated fields (we noted this may require prompt engineering + eval harness).

4) Deployment topology constraints
- Private VPC or dedicated cluster required for production (PHI).
- Sandbox/hybrid approach acceptable: hosted for dev, Dedicated/Private for prod.
- Regional preference: us-west-2 for latency and data residency.

5) Preliminary Redwood proposal (high level)
- Proof-of-concept: Redwood Hosted endpoint (sandbox) + Dedicated pool for limited production rollout.
- Dedicated topology: 2 node pool (8xA100-equivalent) with autoscale to 4 for burst windows; auto-routing to a lower-cost quantized variant when under pressure.
- KV prefix caching enabled for recurrent patient templates; 48-hour cache TTL.
- Monitoring: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95/p99 dashboards, and audit log integration with your Splunk instance.

Attachments: attached a sample CSV with latency traces you shared (pavilion_latency_samples.csv) and a simple sketch of the proposed topology (redwood_deploy_sketch_v1.pdf).

Next steps (suggested)
- Marcus/Neha: I’ll loop them in to produce a one-page architecture + cost envelope. (target: 48 business hours)
- Pavilion: confirm whether the 180-day retention + KMS requirement is mandatory for initial prod (yes/no).
- Schedule a 30-min joint spike to validate p95/p99 on a 13B quantized candidate — propose Wed 14 Jul, 10:00am PT.

If anything above is off, flag and I’ll update.

Hi team — quick technical deep dive and a proposed test plan.

Assumptions based on your samples:
- Average prompt length (post-trimming) ~420 tokens.
- Typical response length ~120 tokens.
- Burst window defined as 10x baseline request rate for ~3–6 minutes.

Proposed dedicated topology (detailed):
- Prod: Dedicated pool with 2 high-memory GPU nodes (48 GB GPU memory class) each hosting 3 model worker replicas (small sharding/replica mix) — target steady throughput 2000 tokens/sec aggregated.
- Autoscale policy: scale to 4 nodes if sustained 95th percentile throughput exceeds 1.8k tokens/sec for >60s; burst fallback routes to a quantized 4-bit variant of the same model.
- Routing: latency-first rule for the summarization route; cost-first for nightly batch jobs.
- KV caching: warm-cache p95 expected ~220 ms; cold-cache p95 can rise to ~520 ms on first interactions for the 70B-class weight. We will instrument client-side prewarming to reduce cold-start tail.
- Sequence length compaction: we recommend prefix-hashing + truncation heuristics for historical notes to cut avg tokens by ~12% without quality loss.

Validation plan (POC spike):
- Step 1 (48h): baseline hosted test on 13B quantized model to validate throughput and p95.
- Step 2 (72h): deploy to Dedicated pool (2-node) and run synthetic bursts (10x) to measure p99 tail and autoscale behavior.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99, token cost per route, cache hit ratio, memory pressure events, and number of fallback invocations.

Deliverables from Redwood after spike:
- One-page architecture + recommended node sizing.
- Empirical latency/throughput report (CSV).
- Cost envelope for steady-state and burst scenarios.

Open questions for Pavilion:
- Is the autoscale latency SLO (time-to-scale) for you: acceptable at 45–60s? If not, we need to provision larger baseline capacity.
- Are there specific encryption/HSM constraints for key usage (we support both KMS and HSM integrations)?

I’ll prepare the architecture doc and a minimal test script (k6-based) if you can give an OK on the proposed spike window.

Thanks,
Marcus
